chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: The first Jazz at the Philharmonic, the Messner brothers and the two-bass solo
summary: He recalls the first concert at the Philharmonic with Nat Cole and Illinois Jacquet, records released on Aladdin, and his two-bass solo with Johnny Miller.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans

blocks.x: That was somewhere in the Porties, during this same period, as a matter of fact. Because this was way before Jazz at the Philharmonic. I remember that, because I was one of the first... Well, we did the first one ever. Nat Cole and Les Paul (he called himself "Paul Leslie" to get away with it), Shorty Sherrock, Jack McVea, Illinois Jacquet, Lee Young. Nat played piano; he called himself "Shorty Nadine" on the records that were released from that. And this was done down on 5th Street, huh, at the Philharmonic. I remember the Messner Brothers had a record store right next to it. That's how our first records were released on Aladdin. This was before Norman had his own label.
I think Reb Spikes mentioned it. Reb said he used to rent that hall to Norman Granz for those...
And he had some association with the Messner brothers, too.
Well, this was before... Eddie and Leo Messner; I was trying to remember their names. This was

before the Jazz at the Philharmonic down on Fifth Street. It was a Baptist organization, as I remember, and I don't know how they consented to Jazz, but this was the reason Norman took it on the road, because they no longer consented to have Jazz played in the Philharmonic.
As I remember that, wasn't there somebody who got excited and cut up some seats one night at a concert, and then they wouldn't let Norman have the auditorium again.
But he kept the name anyway.

He kept the name and he took it on the road, and that's when he brought in Coleman Hawkins, Little Jazz, and Ray Brown, Dizzy Gillespie and all of the new crowd... Oscar Peterson. But anyhow, I had the distinction of being on the first one. There were two bass players, Johnny Miller and I, and we did a two-bass solo on "I Found A New Baby." I'll never forget that, in D-minor.
